moat_against: Structurally thin economics: gross margin 7.8-8.8% FY21-FY25, operating margin ~4-5% — cost pass-through, no real pricing power
Programs are re-biddable and insourceable; Jabil, Flex and Celestica offer near-identical capabilities at greater scale
Customer concentration: top 10 were 51.7% of FY2025 revenue pre-ZT; post-ZT exposure concentrates further in a few hyperscale/AI programs
ZT revenue is lumpy and platform-dependent (Q2 FY26 $1.88B vs Q3 FY26 $1.1B) and rides the NVIDIA-to-AMD platform transition
Working capital absorbs cash exactly when growth accelerates — FY2023 OE/share was -$0.11 in a WC-build year
moat_for: ROIC proxy mid-teens through a cycle (FY21-FY25: 14.8% / 17.0% / 18.2% / 12.2% / 14.5%) on an asset-light, working-capital-disciplined model
Vertically integrated components (PCBs, backplanes, optical transceivers, enclosures) plus design/NPI services raise switching friction vs pure assembly rivals
Qualified, sticky programs in regulated markets — medical, defense, industrial/energy were 62% of FY2025 revenue
ZT Systems adds rack-scale AI integration (liquid cooling, power) and preferred-manufacturer status with AMD; US/Mexico footprint suits defense and reshoring demand
moat_justification: Weak moat: mid-teens ROIC through a cycle and sticky complex/regulated programs plus ZT rack-scale integration, but 8-9% gross margins, no pricing power, re-biddable programs and rising hyperscaler concentration cap it.
name: Sanmina Corporation
one_liner: Real but thin-moat EMS cash generator, moat 4/10, transformed by ZT Systems — even on a cyclically flattering TTM base of $9.15/sh the weighted IRR is only 8.7% at $175.67; it clears 15% only below ~$85.
